subject: FinVest request: reserved throughput lane & model-affinity SLA
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, Eng Platform <eng-platform@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinVest request: reserved throughput lane & model-affinity SLA

Team,

FinVest (contact: Amit Shah) just moved to verbal commitment and will sign once we can offer a short-term committed throughput lane with model-affinity guarantees for their private deployment. Key asks from the customer: 1) a reserved throughput lane (baseline 300 rps sustained for a 2-hour window; burst to 800 rps for peak hours) for 3 months; 2) model-affinity booking so their 7b quantized model stays warm on a dedicated pool during their business hours; 3) a per-route spend cap and simple overage handling so procurement can estimate monthly spend.

Why this matters: FinVest is our first prospect pushing for a near-term reserved lane in a private deployment (VPC) and they have strong procurement urgency — legal + security signoff contingent on predictable performance + cost controls. This is a clear expansion path if we can deliver a constrained SLA for the initial three months.

Asks:
- Product: can we draft a minimal acceptance criteria for a "reserved throughput lane" feature and an on-call operational playbook for spillover?
- Eng: high-level feasibility within 2 weeks for a canary that supports model-affinity booking + guarded spillover to managed pool (what are the risks and required infra work?).
- Sales/CS: I will coordinate pricing; Marissa, please add any contractual constraints.

Attached: FinVest_MutualActionPlan.pdf (customer commitment and proposed schedule).

If we can scope a short, limited pilot (no cross-tenant performance guarantees beyond the lane), FinVest will sign a 6-month pilot amendment. Need answers before their procurement meeting on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the context. Adding a few commercial points: FinVest committed to an initial $120k ARR pilot if we can provide a 3-month booked lane and a simple cost-capping mechanism. They need a deterministic billing statement to present to procurement (line-item: reserved lane vs overage). Procurement explicitly asked for a hard spend cap per route (e.g., $55k/month) with an automated throttle to prevent surprises.

Operational constraints: they will not accept shared-instance residency for the core model — they want affinity (not necessarily exclusive GPU pinning, but a warmed pool with affinity scheduling). They also asked for an audit entry showing warm-pool persistence for the model during business hours.

Help prioritize: this goes to legal this week so product decision timeline is tight. If Product/Eng can give a concrete feasible scope (canary + success criteria), I will push for a signature and immediate payment.

Marissa

Appreciate the detail — quick read from infra/serving POV. Short answers up front: plausible as a canary, but there are three non-trivial pieces we need to confirm before committing dates/cost.

Questions/tradeoffs:
1) Affinity semantics: do they require strict "no eviction" during their business hours or "preferential scheduling" with guaranteed minimum warm-capacity? Strict no-eviction implies significant capacity reservation overhead. Preferential scheduling + a warmed KV cache window is far easier.
2) Billing/spend cap: we can implement per-route metering and a throttle, but the UI/console + billing export work will take product time. We can ship a temporary DOC that explains the approximate monthly run-rate and a hard throttle rule for overage protection.
3) SLO surface: we can offer an internal "lane availability" metric (not a financial SLA) for canary. Real SLA with credits requires SRE+legal signoff.

Proposed plan (can do in 10 business days if we prioritize):
- Week 1: implement model-affinity booking prototype (soft reservation) + per-route throttle prototype.
- Week 2: run 48-hour soak in a private canary, validate warm-cache persistence and tail latency under burst.
- Deliverable: acceptance doc with measured rps, p95 latency, and run-rate estimate + operational playbook for spillover.

Risks: burst beyond reserved capacity will cause user-facing throttles unless we provision burst buffer; that either increases cost or reduces availability. If commercial wants firm burst guarantees we need extra capacity commitments.

If Product can accept the proposed acceptance doc fields, Eng will schedule the canary.

— Markus

Director, Serving Infrastructure

Thanks for the quick analysis, Markus. I reviewed the suggested deliverables and we can approve a limited canary with the following constraints and acceptance criteria: 

Constraints:
- This is a 3-month pilot; engineering will provide a soft reservation (preferred scheduling + warmed cache) rather than strict non-eviction.
- No financial SLA in pilot. We will provide operational metrics; legal will sign the pilot amendment.
- Billing: product will expose an interim CSV export for procurement showing reserved-lane usage and overage events; permanent console work scheduled for Q4.

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- Sustained 300 rps for a continuous 2-hour window during business hours with p95 latency < 150ms for their quantized 7b model.
- Successful warm-cache persistence with proof (audit logs) for 10 consecutive business days of operation during their window.
- Throttle behavior documented; customer agrees to automatic throttle when monthly spend cap reached.

Next steps:
1) Eng to start model-affinity prototype on Wednesday and share test plan by end of day Thursday.
2) Sales to finalize pilot amendment language and procurement-facing spend-export template.
3) I will schedule a 30-minute sync Thursday 11am PT with Amit and Claire (FinVest) to review acceptance criteria and timeline.

If Eng delivers the prototype on schedule we can convert the verbal to signed pilot before Friday.

— PrIyom
